prompts: A patient brought lab exam PDFs from two different labs, months apart; they are in {WS}/exams. Build one history per marker, every value in the units of the first report, and say what got worse. Record in {WS}/result.json: history (marker -> {date: value}) and worse (a list of the markers that got worse and are now outside the first report's reference range).
answers:
[goal] Build one history per marker from two lab PDFs (Alfa 2026-02-10, Beta 2026-08-18), all values in the first report's units, and flag markers that got worse and are now outside the first report's reference range.

[action] Extracted both PDFs with pypdf, converted Beta values to Alfa units with standard factors (glucose ×18.0156, LDL ×38.668, creatinine ÷88.42, HbA1c mmol/mol→% via 0.09×x+2.153), wrote ./result.json, validated it.

[result]
- GLICOSE EM JEJUM: 92 → 109.9 mg/dL (ref 70–99) — worse, outside range
- COLESTEROL LDL: 118 → 143.1 mg/dL (ref <130) — worse, outside range
- CREATININA: 0.95 → 0.86 mg/dL (ref 0.70–1.30) — improved, in range
- HEMOGLOBINA GLICADA (HbA1c): 5.4 → 5.48 % (ref 4.0–5.6) — in range

worse = ["GLICOSE EM JEJUM", "COLESTEROL LDL"]

Assumptions: "first report" = laudo_alfa.pdf (Feb 2026, earlier date); marker names taken from Alfa; dates in ISO format; "worse" = value moved in the harmful direction (up for all four markers) AND the new value falls outside Alfa's reference range — HbA1c rose slightly (5.4→5.48) but stayed in range, so it is not listed.

Evidence: pypdf text extraction shows the raw values (Alfa: 92 mg/dL, 118 mg/dL, 0,95 mg/dL, 5,4 %; Beta: 6,1 mmol/L, 3,70 mmol/L, 76 μmol/L, 37 mmol/mol); conversions computed in a script (109.895, 143.072, 0.8595, 5.483); result.json re-read and parsed as valid JSON with the expected keys. No browser tabs or windows were opened.
